description: A drop of water that will not evaporate or spill. Dewling wears one like a crown and guards it badly.
lore: A drop that keeps its curve keeps it exactly, so what you get looking through one at arm's length is the far side of the valley, small and bright and upside down. Cutlers use them to check an edge. [[characters/a6d7323d|Gunnar]] uses his to read his own far stakes without walking to them, which takes the eastern line from three days down to one. He buys at the wet-field stall, eighteen gold, off whatever the crackers bring in from the [[monsters/forest_poring|Dewlings]], and he buys one a year, every year, because the neck clouds over by autumn and he will not measure through a clouded one. The stallholder keeps the tally out of politeness and has never once been asked for it. Last spring he came back inside the same season and bought a second.
gm_notes: Ships nothing new: Gunnar's yearly eastern line and his silence are already in his dossier. The tally is the tell — a second drop in one season means he measured twice, and the only reason he measures twice is that a number came back worse. Give the stall tally to a player who thinks to ask; it is a date, not an answer, and it is the cheapest way to put his clock in a player's hand.
